original.description: The aviator Marcel Brindejonc des Moulinais (1892–1916) preparing to leave on reconnaissance, with five bombs on the ground at his feet. Catalogued by the Bibliothèque nationale de France under the subject headings for Brindejonc des Moulinais, First World War aviation, military aircraft, pilots and bombs, reference Rol 42922, October 1914.
original.photographer: Agence Rol (press agency; the operator is not named)
original.archive: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Agence Rol collection, reference Rol 42922; digitised on Gallica (btv1b69323418), via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: public domain (Commons record: LicenseShortName "Public domain"; UsageTerms "Public domain"). Credit line on the record: Bibliothèque nationale de France.

colorization.status: not colorized. Recommendation: leave as it is if the Langle de Cary photograph is colorized for the same card.

content_policy: ok — an airman beside his aircraft with unfused bombs on the ground; no casualties, nothing of what the bombs did
caption: The airman Marcel Brindejonc des Moulinais before a reconnaissance flight, October 1914, with the five bombs he would drop by hand at his feet. He was a pre-war record-breaker; he was killed in 1916.
credit: Original photograph: Agence Rol, October 1914; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Rol 42922, via Gallica and Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. Shows what an aeroplane was in 1914: a man, a machine and five bombs he threw over the side. No Royal Flying Corps photograph of 1914 was found under an admissible licence during this pass — see the gaps section of docs/imagery-phase-1.md.
